title: Qwen Envoy · v5
summary: A small adapter trained to investigate papers through Python tools and submit cited answers.

training.Objective: Predict the next Python action or final submission; prior context is masked
training.Targets: q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj

dataset.Source: QASPER official training split; paper-disjoint train/validation
dataset.Preparation: Recorded teacher trajectories plus reviewed, re-executed repairs
dataset.Review: Assistant-reviewed with references visible; not independent human review
dataset.Exposure: Own data split recorded; upstream Qwen training-paper membership unknown

conclusion: Better execution reliability in this run; no demonstrated improvement in substantive paper answering.
limitations: The September 30 comparison uses 40 QASPER-derived questions. References and semantic grades are not independently validated. No model promotion is claimed.
The shared 8,192-token serving cap contributed to 11 base context failures. This is a model-plus-harness observation, not a general reasoning claim.
Checkpoint-50 was selected near the epoch-two validation-loss minimum and checked on development questions; it is not the final 108-step checkpoint.
The training manifest records a script hash but no git commit. The current training script differs; the recorded recipe is not a bit-for-bit reproducibility guarantee.
A user-uploaded paper run uses the public-paper product prompt and discovery checks. It is a separate unreviewed workload, not another score in the frozen benchmark.
The prefix-cache experiment is prepared, not measured. No speedup or complete historical base/v5 cost comparison is claimed.
